clauses.source: Hilbert frequency extension and intersection of real weighted targets
clauses.scope: Every actual real physical distribution pair in FL²; every r in (1,infinity], including infinity. A real analytic map into the native real ell^(-1,r) space has the same raw normalized frequency coordinates. At every original H^(3/2) source, every coordinate equals the independent normalized physical H4 action derivative, including all closed actions. Equality of the raw coordinates across all r describes one map with values in the target intersection.

clauses.source: Real analytic extension for every finite p>2
clauses.scope: Every finite ENNReal exponent p>2; literal complex target ell^(-1,p/2), with the Banach lower bound proved from p>2. The full original real FL^p pair space maps real analytically to this target. Equal physical distributions give the same Hilbert frequency coordinates and the same independent original-domain physical action derivatives.

At every real physical FL^p pair, p finite and p>2, an open complex neighborhood is fixed first, followed by one ell^(p/3) remainder map and one OnePlus remainder map. The maps precede every finite q>1; their respective quasi-norm and q-norm bounds are locally uniform. At every n!=0 the normalized frequency plus 12*pi*n times the actual product of the fixed Theorem 1.2 Birkhoff coordinates equals n times the sum of these remainders.

qualifications: The fixed Hilbert Birkhoff family uses the same accepted intrinsic manuscript reference as the verified Theorem 1.2.

The printed n-times-remainder expression is an asymptotic as |n| tends to infinity. The Lean asymptotic clause is stated at n!=0. The exact all-index reconstruction is separately proved in physicalFourthFrequencyCandidate_remainder with the actual singleton contribution at n=0; no general complex zero-frequency vanishing is asserted.
The ell^(p/3) component retains its quasi-norm when 2<p<3; no Banach assumption is inserted.

The physical lower Hamiltonians are independently defined mass and momentum on the original full fractional source and calibrated against the Riccati hierarchy; they are not defined by rearranging the desired frequency identity.
